ownerDecision.request: now make a super modernized hypotehtical version a tier 9 and a tier 10
ownerDecision.scope: Two fictional Brazilian game designs on the surviving Osório P.2 of the 266 Brazil line (profiles/osorio.ts marks t3 and t4): the EE-T3 Osório (tier IX) and the EE-T4 Osório (tier X), continuing Engesa's numbering. No such vehicles were built; their photo packets (docs/references/photos/ee-t3-osorio-concept-20261030.json, ee-t4-osorio-concept-20261030.json) cite the P.2 photographs the base follows.

drums.request: add two big fuel barrels on the backs here
drums.scope: Both marks carry two 200 L fuel drums across the stern (the owner chose the EE-T3 and EE-T4 the same day); the envelopes are re-measured with them.

raised.request: raise the drums on the eet3 and eet4 so theyre visible in the hero images a lil more!!! just rule of cool type stuf
raised.scope: The drums stand 31 cm over the deck line; the gun's depression over the stern is re-measured against them.

chevrons.request: for the eet3 osorio, osorio t4, make the front turret attachment things in front of cheeks chevrons like the leopard 2a4 instead of those weird add ons because they look kind of goofy. also add more add ons attachments and tank decorations on all brazilian tanks.
chevrons.scope: The cheek modules become chevron wedges on the Leopard 2A4M pattern (our plain 2A4 keeps the square block; the arrowhead is the 2A4M's 2A6-look front, profiles/leopard2A4Wedge.ts), built in profiles/osorioChevron.ts; the side armour's front pack ends square at their roots. The crew's kit is added through the decoration layer on all eight Brazilian ids.

mantlets.request: for the eet3 and ee4 make their mantelts different but also make both actually match up and align with the cheeks; then "the eet3 mantlet is just flat and horizontal. fix both so theyre more like the leopard 2 mantlets in how they also match the top and bottom angle o the turrets/cheeks" and "it looks like the mantlets guns dont look properly attached"
mantlets.scope: Each mark's mantlet becomes one block riding the gun that fills the slot between its chevron wedges wall to wall, as the Leopard 2A5/2A6's mantlet wedge does: its top is the chevrons' own top carried across the slot (their front slope rising to the roof, meeting in a low ridge over the gun), its underside beside the gun their rising floor, its nose at their tips, and the gun leaves through a collar and seal ring. The EE-T3's is a pointed wedge, its faces parallel to the chevrons' faces; the EE-T4's a flat bolted face square to the gun, gabled on the two planes. The brow is dropped; the gun cradle's round housing about the trunnion axis closes the gun line behind the mantlet. Under the gun each traces the old mount's round underside, so the published gun-depression curves hold (tools/gun-depression-sweep.mjs).

ee_t3_osorio.silhouette: Fictional Brazilian modernization of the surviving Osório P.2 (tier IX): the P.2's low welded hull and wedge turret under a bolted composite nose module and five composite skirt modules a side, chevron wedges over the turret cheeks (the Leopard 2A4M's arrowhead, carrying the side armour's face forward to a blunt tip beside the mantlet), three bolted side packs a side, a PERI-pattern commander's panoramic sight, a deeper rear basket with stowage, set-in nose lamps, the 120 mm L/47 in a pointed mantlet wedge filling the slot between the chevrons to their tips, the roof 7.62 mm, two 200 L fuel drums across the stern in a cradle off the rear plate, standing over the deck line and a three-tone blotch coat.

ee_t4_osorio.silhouette: Fictional Brazilian modernization of the Osório P.2 (tier X), the EE-T3's kit heavier and full length: a nose module carried down a bolted lower-glacis slab with the lamps set in its face, thicker skirt modules, longer, broader chevron wedges with a taller blunt face beside the mantlet, a flat bolted mantlet module filling the slot between the chevrons, flush with their tips, thicker side packs, a hard-kill active protection system (four radar panels on the turret corners, two drum launchers on pedestals), laser-warning heads, a slat cage over the rear plate with two 200 L fuel drums in a cradle behind it, standing over the deck line, the 130 mm L/51 and a three-tone digital coat.
